traps.note: Each band includes its lower bound and excludes its upper one (-<), and '1000 - high' includes 1000. LOW does not match a missing numeric, so a missing written_eur falls to OTHER and gets 'UNKNOWN'. The CASE WHEN must spell out every boundary and send NULL to 'UNKNOWN'.
NODUPKEY keeps each policy's first transaction in load order (the stable sort), and that row sets the band. Spark needs a window ordered by load order (_row_seq), not dropDuplicates.
A one-to-many MERGE with an IN= subset is a left join from txn to policy_band. lob_code and prem_band come only from policy_band and stay missing for unmatched keys.

PROC MEANS NWAY with CLASS drops rows whose lob_code or prem_band is missing, but a Spark groupBy keeps NULL groups. Those groups must be filtered out. N() and SUM() are named by the OUTPUT statement.
The second PROC MEANS NWAY counts policies per lob_code/prem_band and also excludes missing class values, which Spark's groupBy would keep.

merge work.policy_counts work.premium_sums;

traps.note: A MERGE with no IN= keeps keys from both inputs, so it acts as a full outer join on lob_code and prem_band. Columns missing on one side stay missing, and the output is ordered by the BY keys.
&as_of is a SAS date number (days since 1960-01-01). In Spark it must be turned into a DATE, e.g. date_add('1960-01-01', as_of).

contracts.grain: One row per line of business and premium band. Each policy is put in one band, based on the written premium of its first transaction in load order, and all of that policy's transactions are summed in that band.

defects.title: Policies with missing lob_code silently dropped by PROC MEANS CLASS
defects.description: Both PROC MEANS steps use CLASS lob_code prem_band without the MISSING option, so SAS discards every observation whose class variable is missing. lob_code comes from each policy's first-loaded transaction (work.policy_band), so when that row has a blank lob_code, all of that policy's transactions and the policy itself are left out of rpt.premium_band_summary. Written and earned premium are understated.
defects.intended_behaviour: Every transaction should be reported. Policies with a missing line of business should appear in their own (blank or UNKNOWN) lob_code group, for example via the CLASS ... / MISSING option, rather than being dropped.
defects.impact_query: WITH o AS (SELECT policy_id, lob_code, written_eur, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY policy_id ORDER BY _row_seq) AS rn FROM dw_fact_premium_earned), pb AS (SELECT policy_id, lob_code, CASE WHEN written_eur IS NULL THEN 'UNKNOWN' WHEN written_eur < 0 THEN 'NEGATIVE' WHEN written_eur < 250 THEN '0-249' WHEN written_eur < 500 THEN '250-499' WHEN written_eur < 1000 THEN '500-999' ELSE '1000+' END AS prem_band FROM o WHERE rn = 1) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT pb.prem_band) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(ABS(SUM(t.written_eur)), 0) AS amount_affected FROM dw_fact_premium_earned t JOIN pb ON t.policy_id = pb.policy_id WHERE pb.lob_code IS NULL OR TRIM(pb.lob_code) = ''

defects.title: No as-of cut-off: transactions after the reporting date included
defects.description: The as_of parameter is only stamped onto the output (line 74). Nothing filters dw.fact_premium_earned to transactions on or before the reporting date, so transactions dated after 2025-12-31 are counted in n_transactions, written_eur and earned_eur.
defects.intended_behaviour: Only transactions with txn_date on or before &as_of (2025-12-31) should be included in the report as at that date.

defects.title: Policy band taken from first-loaded row, not the earliest (opening) transaction
defects.description: PROC SORT NODUPKEY BY policy_id keeps whichever transaction was loaded first for each policy, and that row's written_eur (and lob_code) sets the band for all the policy's transactions. If the load order differs from transaction order, a later endorsement, cancellation or negative adjustment can set the band, and the policy moves to a different band (or line of business), possibly NEGATIVE.
defects.intended_behaviour: Band each policy on its true opening transaction: the earliest txn_date, with load order breaking ties.
defects.impact_query: WITH r AS (SELECT policy_id, lob_code, written_eur, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY policy_id ORDER BY _row_seq) AS rn_load, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY policy_id ORDER BY txn_date ASC NULLS LAST, _row_seq) AS rn_date FROM dw_fact_premium_earned), b AS (SELECT policy_id, rn_load, rn_date, lob_code, CASE WHEN written_eur IS NULL THEN 'UNKNOWN' WHEN written_eur < 0 THEN 'NEGATIVE' WHEN written_eur < 250 THEN '0-249' WHEN written_eur < 500 THEN '250-499' WHEN written_eur < 1000 THEN '500-999' ELSE '1000+' END AS band FROM r WHERE rn_load = 1 OR rn_date = 1), p AS (SELECT policy_id, MAX(CASE WHEN rn_load = 1 THEN lob_code END) AS l_lob, MAX(CASE WHEN rn_load = 1 THEN band END) AS l_band, MAX(CASE WHEN rn_date = 1 THEN lob_code END) AS i_lob, MAX(CASE WHEN rn_date = 1 THEN band END) AS i_band FROM b GROUP BY policy_id), d AS (SELECT * FROM p WHERE NOT (l_lob <=> i_lob AND l_band <=> i_band)), g AS (SELECT l_lob AS lob, l_band AS band FROM d WHERE l_lob IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(l_lob) <> '' UNION SELECT i_lob, i_band FROM d WHERE i_lob IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(i_lob) <> '') SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM g) AS rows_affected, COALESCE((SELECT SUM(ABS(t.written_eur)) FROM dw_fact_premium_earned t JOIN d ON t.policy_id = d.policy_id), 0) AS amount_affected

tests.description: One policy per row, each with written_eur exactly on or just beside a band edge: -10.00 and -0.01 (NEGATIVE), 0.00 (lower bound of 0-249, included), 249.99 and 250.00 (either side of the 250 edge), 499.99 and 500.00, 999.99, 1000.00 (included in 1000+) and 1000.01. A naive CASE WHEN that uses <= instead of < on the upper bounds, or > 1000 for the top band, puts 0, 250, 500 or 1000 in the wrong band. written_eur is NOT NULL here, so the NULL-to-UNKNOWN branch can't be reached with legal inputs.

Three policies, each with several transactions in different bands. For every policy, the first row in load order is not the row with the lowest txn_id or the earliest txn_date, and it falls in a different band from those rows. Policy rows are also interleaved in load order. NODUPKEY bands each policy on its first loaded row. dropDuplicates (arbitrary row), or a window ordered by txn_id or txn_date, picks another row and moves all of that policy's transactions to another band.

Lines 50-52: some policies have transactions loaded with a different lob_code from their first (opening) row. Policy 301 opens as MOTOR and later has HOME rows. Policy 302 opens as HOME and later has a MOTOR row. Policy 303 has a single PROP row. The MERGE takes lob_code and prem_band only from policy_band (txn keeps no lob_code), so every transaction is reported under the opening row's lob_code and band. A naive join that keeps the transaction's own lob_code, or groups on it, splits these policies across LOBs and changes n_transactions and the sums.

Lines 71-72: rows are loaded in no particular order and cover several LOBs, each with several bands, including NEGATIVE and 1000+. The final MERGE BY lob_code prem_band is a full outer join, and its output is sorted by the BY keys, with prem_band sorted as text ('0-249' < '1000+' < '250-499' < '500-999' < 'NEGATIVE'). A naive translation using an inner join, an unordered result, or numeric band order gives different output. Policy 405 has two transactions, so n_policies and n_transactions differ in its group.

A few policies whose input as_of_date column holds 2025-11-30, not the run parameter AsOfDate=2025-12-31. The output as_of_date must be the SAS date number &as_of turned into the DATE 2025-12-31. A naive translation that puts the raw integer in the column, adds it to the wrong epoch (1970-01-01), or carries over the input table's as_of_date gives a different value.

n_transactions counts only non-missing written_eur values. It is not a row count.

The final merge on lob_code and prem_band is a full match and drops nothing.

warnings:
translator notes: - I take load order to be _row_seq (the lineage agent's inference, confidence 0.55). It decides which row sets each policy's band and lob_code.
- lob_code is right-trimmed, and a blank value is treated as missing, as SAS does. The CLASS filter then drops those policies (S03-D1).
- Missing policy_id values form one group: the window partition keeps them together and the join uses null-safe equality, as SAS BY-group matching does.
- n_transactions is N(written_eur), the count of non-missing values, not a row count. n_policies is N(policy_id).
- Sums are taken in double precision. Spark's summation order is not defined, so the last bits may differ slightly from SAS's sequential sum. Check that reconciliation allows a float tolerance.
- AsOfDate is read as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text. If it is ever passed as a SAS day number, it is converted with date_add('1960-01-01', n).
